newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher despite softer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher despite softer cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Thursday ahead of the Easter holiday weekend despite softer cash market prices and expectations of more generation capacity returning on line next week.
Most market sources attributed today's gain to covering of short positions amid the lack of fresh fundamental news.
"There were a few people who were short and did not want to worry ahead of the long weekend," said a Houston trader.
NYMEX will close tomorrow in observance of Good Friday.

May California-Oregon Border (COB) futures ended up 22 cents at $10.70 a megawatt hour (MWh) after traded between $10.40 and $10.70. June COB settled down 17 cents at $10.95. Other active COB contracts ended flat to five cents higher.
May Palo Verde (PV) settled up 33 cents at $15.20 after posting a low of $14.60. June PV finished up 32 cents at $16.21. Other active PV months ended up eight to 15 cents.
Weekday electricity prices for firm, peak delivery at COB was quoted at $11.25-12.00/MWh compared with $11.50-12.00, while those at PV slipped to $14.25-15.50 from yesterday's $14.75-15.75.

"I still think it'll trade lower." the Houston trader said, citing the moderate energy energy, plenty of hydropower in the Northwest and more nuclear generation in Southwest next week as factors which would pressure the complex down.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington will be shut today, several weeks earlier than planned for maintenance due to ample hydropower in the region.
There was also talk of an outage at the 750 MW unit 2 at the Navajo coal-fire plant in Arizona lasting as long as two weeks, although the unit's status could not be confirmed.
Several units were planning to resume generation, with the 1,070 MW San Onofre unit 2 in southern California and the 1,221 MW Palo Verde unit 3 in Arizona scheduled to resume operations next week.

Capacity on the Pacific Intertie power transmission system, which links the Northwest to Southern California, will be raised to 6,250 megawatts by this weekend, if Bonneville Power Administration is successful in re-energizing the 500 KV John Day-Slatt line in Oregon.
In the Northwest, temperatures would remain near normal across the western part of the area until the end of the week, and run little above normal in the south and east.
The Southwest would stay dry and warm into early next week with readings running 4-12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal.

Weather Services Corp said Northwest cities like Portland and Seattle would see readings in the 50s through Saturday, while Southwest centers such as Los Angeles and Phoenix would experience temperatures in the 70s-80s.
NYMEX estimated 235 COB and 465 PV contracts were sold, compared with 169 COB and 516 PV lots Thursday.
